page_title: KRect — Rectangle-style window management for Ubuntu KDE
description: Arrange windows on Ubuntu and Kubuntu KDE with dragging or shortcuts. KRect is a free, open-source app with a top snap bar, 18 actions, and landscape and portrait monitor support.
hero_description: Rectangle-style window management for Ubuntu KDE. Drag a window into place or use a shortcut to organize your workspace.
hero_note: 0.3.1: fixes for snap bar visibility and stacking
demo_note: Press a button to try a layout. This is a browser illustration.
features_intro: Window placement runs inside KWin. A native Qt app puts the controls in your hands.
feature_1_title: From half a screen to portrait thirds
feature_1_body: 18 window actions and movement between displays. Repeat a half shortcut to cycle through ½ → ⅔ → ⅓. On portrait monitors, thirds stack vertically.
feature_2_title: Respect the panels. Keep your shortcuts.
feature_2_body: KRect uses KDE's work areas to leave panels clear. Edit global shortcuts in the app and check for conflicts before saving.
feature_3_body: Arrange your last work window from the app or tray, or drag it into place. Set your preferred window gaps, excluded apps, and login behavior.
screenshot_alt: The real KRect Qt app, showing landscape and portrait monitors and window layout buttons
screenshot_caption: KRect 0.2.0 on Plasma 5.27 / X11. The app supports Korean and English.
download_intro: No account. No payment. Choose the package for your Ubuntu version and get started.
compatibility_body: Requires a KDE Plasma 5.27 or 6 session on Ubuntu or Kubuntu. GNOME is not supported.
validation_body: Tested on a real Plasma 5.27 / X11 desktop. Live Plasma 6 / Wayland sessions and mixed scaling still need validation.
free_note: Get the .deb file without an account or payment.
copy_failed: Select and copy the command manually.
install_help: Run this in your download folder. Then find KRect in the app launcher and click ‘Enable KRect’.
faq_1_answer: Yes. KRect is free and open source under the MIT license. Every feature is available without restrictions. The source and release files are available on GitHub.
faq_2_question: Will it work on regular Ubuntu?
faq_2_answer: You need a KDE Plasma session. The default GNOME desktop is not supported. On Kubuntu or Ubuntu with KDE installed, check your version with plasmashell --version.
faq_3_question: How do I update an existing installation?
faq_3_answer: Quit KRect from its tray menu, install the new .deb, then reopen the app. If you installed from source, remove that user copy with bash uninstall.sh in its source folder first. User installations take priority over system packages.
faq_4_question: Is this the same app as Rectangle?
faq_4_answer: KRect is an independent implementation inspired by Rectangle, adapted for KDE panels, portrait monitors, and global shortcuts. Version 0.3.0 adds dragging to a top snap bar. Custom layout presets are not included yet.
footer_note: Inspired by Rectangle. Made for KDE. Not an official Rectangle or KDE product.
faq_5_question: Why does the snap bar not appear?
faq_5_answer: Enable KRect and keep it running in the tray. Turn on drag layouts in Preferences, then drag a movable window to the top center of a display. Hovering over the maximize button is not supported.
snap_intro: Choose a layout at the top of your screen, without memorizing a shortcut.
snap_step_1: Grab the title bar and drag the window to the top center of a display.
snap_step_2: Move into a region on the snap bar to preview its destination.
snap_step_3: Release the mouse to place the window in that region.
snap_cancel: Leave the bar to continue dragging. Press Esc to cancel, or use the restore shortcut to return to the previous position.
snap_requirement: Keep KRect running in the tray. You can turn drag layouts off in Preferences.
snap_landscape_alt: Actual KRect snap bar with horizontal and vertical halves, thirds, asymmetric thirds, and quarters. The left half is selected.
snap_landscape_caption: Landscape · Halves, thirds, two thirds, and quarters.
snap_portrait_alt: Actual KRect snap bar on a portrait monitor, with vertically stacked thirds and the center region selected.
snap_portrait_caption: Portrait · Thirds and two thirds stack vertically.
snap_proof: Real snap bars captured on Plasma 5.27 / X11. KRect follows your KDE theme and configured window gaps.
